get.description: Returns the private profile of the account owning the token: id, username, e-mail, CPU, badge, GCL/power progress, credit balance (`money`), notification preferences, linked Steam data and power-creep experimentation state. screeps.com additionally returns shard CPU limits (`cpuShard`, `cpuShardUpdatedTime`), account resources, SSO links and legacy fields; OpenScreeps never returns those and instead mirrors the backend-local projection (`emailDirty`, `lastChargeTime`, `blocked`, `customBadge`). Only fields present in storage are serialized. The official client uses this endpoint only for full-access tokens; restricted tokens resolve the user through `GET /api/user/name` + `GET /api/user/find`.

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope.

x-observations.notes: Authenticated read-only response represents steam.ownership as an array of integer Steam application IDs, unlike the standalone boolean. No account identifiers or credentials are recorded.

x-compatibility.openscreeps: Token may be sent as `X-Token`, `Authorization: Bearer`, or `?token=`; each authenticated call issues a fresh token in the `X-Token` response header (default lifetime 60 s).
x-compatibility.screeps-com: Fields such as cpuShard, resources, github/twitter are typed by the official client only.

get.description: Returns the permissions of a screeps.com account auth token: whether it has full access, or the REST endpoints and WebSocket channel groups it is restricted to, plus its description. The official client calls it to decide between `GET /api/auth/me` and the restricted `GET /api/user/name` lookup. Unrecognized tokens produce an HTTP error. Not implemented by OpenScreeps or backend-local, which issue only short-lived full-access session tokens.

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope.

404.description: Route not implemented (OpenScreeps answers Nest's `{message, error: "Not Found", statusCode: 404}`; the official client documents HTTP 404 on unofficial servers for official-only routes).

post.description: Exchanges local credentials for a session token. The `email` field carries an e-mail address or, on OpenScreeps, a username (looked up case-insensitively unless it contains `@`). OpenScreeps verifies scrypt hashes in constant time (unknown accounts still hash a dummy) and answers every failure with HTTP 401 `unauthorized`; accounts without a configured password cannot sign in. The official client notes that password sign-in has not worked on screeps.com since 2018 (use account auth tokens there); it remains the authentication method for private servers.

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope.

400.description: OpenScreeps: malformed JSON (`invalid request`) or a body that is not a JSON object (`invalid params`).

413.description: OpenScreeps: JSON body larger than 8 MB (`request too large`).

x-compatibility.backend-local: The pinned backend-local has no signin route (provided by auth mods on private servers).

post.summary: Sign in with a Steam session ticket
post.description: Verifies a Steam session ticket and returns a session token plus the authenticated SteamID, creating a new account (no username, 100 CPU, default code branch, empty Memory) the first time a SteamID signs in. OpenScreeps verifies the ticket with the Steam Web API `ISteamUserAuth/AuthenticateUserTicket` (app 464350) using the operator-configured Steam Web API key, outside the world lock and with a 10 s timeout; without a configured key, or when `useNativeAuth` is truthy, it answers `authentication method is not supported`. Any verification failure yields `could not authenticate`. The official client documents Steam (and GitHub) SSO as the only sign-in methods on screeps.com but does not type the response.

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope. Known `error` values: `authentication method is not supported`, `could not authenticate`.

400.description: OpenScreeps: malformed JSON (`invalid request`) or a body that is not a JSON object (`invalid params`).

413.description: OpenScreeps: JSON body larger than 8 MB (`request too large`).

x-compatibility.screeps-com: Response typed `ScreepsUnknownResponse` by the official client; token/steamid fields are from backend-local/OpenScreeps.

Without `season`, returns `{list}` of the user's rankings across all seasons. The username is matched case-insensitively; unknown users yield `user not found` on OpenScreeps. backend-local is a stub: with `season` it always answers `result not found`, otherwise an empty list.

post.description: Queues a JavaScript expression for evaluation in the player's runtime, with normal CPU accounting. post.description: screeps.com only. Replaces the account's CPU allocation across shards (`Game.cpu.shardLimits`) with `cpu: {<shard>: limit}`. Observed: the limits must total the account CPU (omitted shards count as 0), and changes made too soon after the previous change are rejected (an interval of about 12 hours was observed; the exact cooldown and its error text are not documented). The new allocation is reflected in `GET /api/auth/me` (`cpuShard`, `cpuShardUpdatedTime`). Note that placing an initial spawn (`gamePlaceSpawn`) resets the allocation to the shard where the spawn was placed. The success body carries `ok: 1` plus database-driver metadata; only `ok` is stable. OpenScreeps has a single world with no shard CPU allocation and does not implement this route.

post.description: Assigns `value` at `path`, deletes the value at `path` when `value` is omitted, or (without `path`) clears Memory and merges an object `value` into it. The edit is not applied synchronously: it is queued as a hidden console command executed inside the player's runtime. Commands are queued and run only when the player's runtime reaches its console-processing step (after a main loop run); no ordering relative to other queued commands, ticks or code deployment is guaranteed by this API, and the response does not contain the evaluation result (results arrive on the console realtime channel). JSON-serialized values over 1 MiB yield `memory size is too large`; OpenScreeps rejects invalid paths (`Incorrect memory path`) and, at execution, fails the hidden command when an intermediate path element is not an object.

get.summary: List rooms where respawning is prohibited
get.description: Lists rooms the player may not choose for a new spawn after respawning. screeps.com returns zero or one `shard/room` entries; OpenScreeps and backend-local always return an empty list.

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope.

get.summary: List rooms claimed by a user
get.description: Public. Lists rooms whose controller the given user owns. screeps.com groups rooms by shard (`shards`) with an always-empty `reservations` map; OpenScreeps and backend-local return a flat `rooms` array sorted by controller level (descending), which the official client maps to `shards.privSrv`. An unknown or missing `id` returns an empty list.

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope.

post.summary: Activate a branch in world or simulator
post.description: Makes the named branch the one running in the world (`activeWorld`) or simulator (`activeSim`), clearing the flag from all other branches, and publishes `user:<id>/set-active-branch`. Activating for the world loads that branch's code into the runtime. Errors: `invalid params` for another `activeName`, `no branch` for an unknown branch.

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope. Known `error` values: `invalid params`, `no branch`.

400.description: OpenScreeps: malformed JSON (`invalid request`) or a body that is not a JSON object (`invalid params`).

413.description: OpenScreeps: JSON body larger than 8 MB (`request too large`).

x-compatibility.screeps-com: screeps.com endpoint limit: 240 requests per day per token (HTTP 429 with `X-RateLimit-Limit`/`-Remaining`/`-Reset`), in addition to the global 120 per minute.

post.summary: Show or hide the Steam profile link
post.description: Controls whether `GET /api/user/find` exposes the linked Steam id. No effect for accounts without a Steam link. Not exposed by the official client, so screeps.com availability is unverified.

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope.

400.description: OpenScreeps: malformed JSON (`invalid request`) or a body that is not a JSON object (`invalid params`).

413.description: OpenScreeps: JSON body larger than 8 MB (`request too large`).

get.description: Public. Sums each room statistic of the user over the selected window (8 = last 8 eight-minute slots, 180 = 8 three-hour slots, 1440 = 7 daily slots on OpenScreeps). Other intervals yield `invalid params`. OpenScreeps requires `id` (this route is unauthenticated, so there is no caller fallback) and answers `user not found` otherwise; backend-local returns empty `stats`.

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope. Known `error` values: `invalid params`, `user not found`.

post.description: Records that the tutorial was completed. OpenScreeps and backend-local accept the call and store nothing.

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope.

400.description: OpenScreeps: malformed JSON (`invalid request`) or a body that is not a JSON object (`invalid params`).

413.description: OpenScreeps: JSON body larger than 8 MB (`request too large`).

get.summary: Get the room to center the map on
get.description: Returns zero or one room name the client should center the world map on when opened without coordinates: a random room whose controller the user owns, otherwise a default start room. Observed on screeps.com: when the `shard` query parameter is omitted, the result may be returned as `shard/room` (the official client documents this format); with `shard`, a plain room name for that shard. OpenScreeps ignores `shard` and returns a plain room name: a random owned-controller room, else `W5N5` if it exists, else the alphabetically first `normal` room (backend-local always falls back to `W5N5`).

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope.

get.description: Returns whether the player must place a first spawn (`empty`), is established (`normal`: owns a spawn in a room whose controller it also owns) or has lost every such spawn (`lost`, may respawn). Observed on screeps.com: the status is account-wide, aggregated across all shards, regardless of any `shard` parameter. OpenScreeps computes it from the single world (no objects → `empty`).

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope.

x-compatibility.screeps-com: Account-wide across shards (observed); see `gamePlaceSpawn` for initial spawn placement.
